Jie Yiguan, courtesy name Zengwei, was a native of Jiaocheng. A jinshi of Zhengde 16, he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Works. He set out ten proposals: explain learning, cultivate virtue, draw near to worthy men, honor parents, appoint ministers, keep villains at a distance, employ remonstrance, make commands careful, restrain desire, and care for the people. Shizong approved and accepted them. In Jiajing 1 he went out with censors to audit horse-pasture lands. The eunuch Yan Hong and others requested that a palace eunuch be sent along, but Yiguan said this could not be allowed, and the matter was dropped. Back at court he impeached the eunuchs Gu Dayong and Li Xi for seizing property and harming the people; the emperor pardoned them, but estates occupied by eunuchs, meritorious nobles, and imperial relatives were generally returned to the people. The emperor built an extremely magnificent residence for Empress Dowager Chen's father, Chen Wanyan. Yiguan strongly urged restraint, and also helped Yang Tinghe oppose the weaving offices, but neither proposal was accepted. He later served as Left and Right Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice. When Guo Nan, regional inspector of Yunnan, was arrested for speaking out; Zhang You, Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, and Vice Commissioner Sun Mao for insulting palace constables; Censor Fang Qiyan lost office for flogging a eunuch's servant to death; and Zhang Haogu, magistrate of Yuancheng, was demoted for detaining and rebuking relatives of an imperial in-law, Yiguan argued to save them all. He offended the throne and had his salary suspended.

The single-character names 錄, 琦, 瓊, 漢, 科 are taken as Ma Lu, Liu Qi, Lu Qiong, Shen Han and Wang Ke per the English and earlier biographies in the chapter.
母後 is the empress dowager invoked by sycophants; the chunk does not name her.
魯迷 is translated as a person, Lu Mi; it is the tribute state Lumi. The candidate is disposed as a polity and a repair is proposed.
崞、洛 are read as the places Guo and Luo(chuan) where the witnesses lived, not people.
李伏答 is the Guo County registration name, read in the English as Li Fuda; it is kept as an alternate name of Li Fuda.
李午 here is an alias of Li Fuda per Xue Liang, distinct from the Li Wu named as Li Tong's grandfather in s0160a.
The English renders 趙鑒 as Li Jian here and in s0419 and s0424; the surfaces follow the current text but link to a separate Zhao Jian row, and repairs are proposed.
驄 is taken as a variant for 璁 (Zhang Cong); the literal reads it as Ye Yingcong. The surface is linked to Zhang Cong with a repair proposed.
後 (the empress, Chen Wanyan's daughter) is not named; her row is labeled Empress Chen from her father's surname.
道聞喪歸 does not say whose death Zheng Luoshu mourned; no relative row is created.
Hu Sen, Yang Lin and Wang Ji are relatives of the chief ministers (輔臣) without saying whether Zhang Cong's or Gui E's; the kin edge is to Gui E as uncertain.

正陽之月 conflicts with the tenth-month date of the eclipse in s0599; the extraction keeps the s0599 date and flags the wording.
